key_observations: The new freelance engagement moved beyond setup into a first concrete implementation slice, with authentication work progressing through code, tests, repository review, and client communication.
The SaaS beta was deliberately kept in observation mode: analytics and user feedback were checked, but no broad feature expansion was started.
The technical YouTube/search session is ambiguous from raw events alone, but in the actual sequence it fed directly into the new client's authentication implementation.
The older freelance project appears to have reached client acceptance, creating a cleaner delivery state while the newer engagement becomes the main freelance workload.
This was a lighter Saturday with meaningful but bounded work and long offline periods.

priority_alignment.assessment: moderate progress / beta monitoring and decision discipline
strong progress / acceptance reached on the older project
limited today; existing pipeline was maintained

important_uncertainty: Client acceptance email indicates the older project moved toward closure, but final payment or administrative closure is not established.
The new client's authentication slice was tested, but the first deliverable is not complete based on the captured work alone.
The SaaS beta feedback and analytics review do not establish whether activation or retention is improving.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Finish the new client's first authentication deliverable while keeping the SaaS beta stable until another meaningful user signal arrives.

primary_action.title: Finish the new client's first deliverable
primary_action.reason: The new client has moved into real implementation and testing, making completion of the initial authentication slice the clearest near-term freelance milestone.

secondary_action.title: Keep the SaaS in observation mode
secondary_action.reason: The beta is producing feedback and analytics that have already shaped recent changes, so another broad feature cycle should wait for more evidence.

things_not_to_do: Do not treat the older client's acceptance email as proof that all administrative closeout is complete.
Do not infer that the technical YouTube session was entertainment just because it occurred on YouTube.
Do not treat the new client's authentication work as finished because tests passed.
Do not add a major SaaS feature while the beta remains in an evidence-gathering phase.
Do not infer anything about the long offline periods beyond the stated unobserved status.
